pull.title: feat(models): one picker entry per tier, in every coding agent
pull.body:
## The asymmetry this closes, measured

Read-only over the live request log (`~/.fcc/logs/requests.db`, `mode=ro`), 272,132 rows:

> **Across the whole history, the number of non-Claude-Code requests that ever named a tier-style
> alias is ZERO.** Every coding-agent request named a concrete `provider/model` ref, because that
> was the only thing that existed for it — while 99.98% of Claude Code traffic names an alias and
> almost never a ref (115,825 alias rows vs 7 gateway-ref rows for `claude-cli` all-time).

Claude Code asks for `claude-sonnet-5` and MCC maps that onto whatever `MODEL_SONNET` points at, so
moving a route moves every session already running on it. A model id typed into OpenCode's config a
month ago is still that id today, however many times the route it should have been following moved.

## What ships

Five names, at the head of the picker MCC generates for each of the **thirteen** agents that carry a
catalogue (codex, pi, opencode, opencode2, kilo, commandcode_cli, kimi_code, qwen_code, crush,
cline_cli, aider, droid, gemini_cli):

| Name | Route it names | Chain it uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mcc/best` | `MODEL` | `MODEL_FALLBACKS`, `MODEL_PAUSED` |
| `mcc/good` | `MODEL_OPUS` | `MODEL_OPUS_FALLBACKS`, `MODEL_OPUS_PAUSED` |
| `mcc/medium` | `MODEL_SONNET` | `MODEL_SONNET_FALLBACKS`, `MODEL_SONNET_PAUSED` |
| `mcc/cheap` | `MODEL_HAIKU` | `MODEL_HAIKU_FALLBACKS`, `MODEL_HAIKU_PAUSED` |
| `mcc/vision` | `MODEL_VISION` | `MODEL_VISION_FALLBACKS`, `MODEL_VISION_PAUSED` |

Pointer semantics, **including the collapse**: on a default install the four optional routes are
unset, so all five resolve to `MODEL` — primary, fallbacks and pause list together — exactly as
`claude-opus-5` already does. MCC does not invent a distinct model for an unset tier; the card says
*"Same as global Opus — currently `<ref>`. MODEL_OPUS is unset, so it follows MODEL."*

Per-agent overrides live in `~/.fcc/harness_tiers.json` (three states per `(agent, tier)`: key
absent = inherit; entry with no `model` = global primary + this agent's own fallbacks; `model` set =
this agent's chain leads) and are edited on the Coding agents card's new **Tiers** section, which
renders the *same* rail component Model Config uses.

## Resolution flow

`ModelRouter.resolve` / `resolve_chain` intercept a tier **before** `_direct_provider_model`.
`mcc/best` already "worked" on `fork/main` — by accident: `mcc` is not a supported provider id, the
direct branch declined it, `_matched_route` matched nothing and `_resolve_model_ref` fell through to
`settings.model` with no fallbacks, no pause and no trace in the log. This **replaces** that, rather
than layering a rule over it.

`application/tier_chains.resolve_tier_chain` is the single rule, with two callers that must never
disagree — the router answering a request, and `catalogue_model.py` writing the alias entry whose
display name states which model the tier points at today. Order: this agent's entry with a `model` →
its chain leads; entry with no `model` → global primary + this agent's fallbacks; otherwise → the
global chain. **An unknown harness takes the third branch** — a raw curl or an old launcher still
gets a working tier, it simply gets the global one.

Both wire spellings parse, because the fleet is split (bare ref from Codex/Command Code/OpenCode/
Kilo/Pi/Kimi, `anthropic/<ref>` from Cline/Crush/Droid/Gemini CLI/Qwen/Aider). The tier segment is
matched **exactly**, never as a substring — `_matched_route` is a substring match, and repeating that
hazard with five more names would be a routing bug nobody could see.

## Proof, on a scratch server

Scratch MCC on `127.0.0.1:8199` with an isolated `HOME`, a two-provider fake gateway on `:8299`
(`custom_alpha`, `custom_beta`). The live `:8082` server was never written to and never restarted.

`GET /v1/models` — both spellings, outside the visibility filter, display names showing the collapse:

```
('mcc/best',   'Best (custom_alpha/alpha-1)')       ('anthropic/mcc/best',   …)
('mcc/good',   'Good (custom_alpha/alpha-1)')       ('anthropic/mcc/good',   …)
('mcc/medium', 'Medium (custom_alpha/alpha-1)')     ('anthropic/mcc/medium', …)
('mcc/cheap',  'Cheap (custom_alpha/alpha-cheap)')  ('anthropic/mcc/cheap',  …)
('mcc/vision', 'Vision (custom_alpha/vision-1)')    ('anthropic/mcc/vision', …)
```

With `harness_tiers.json` giving opencode's BEST `custom_beta/beta-1`:

```
harness=opencode  mcc/best        -> beta-1     (the override)
harness=crush     mcc/best        -> alpha-1    (the global chain)
no harness at all mcc/best        -> alpha-1    (documented fallback)
claude-cli UA     claude-fable-5  -> alpha-1    (untouched)
override primary paused           -> beta-cheap (falls to its own fallback)
mcc/vision + an image part        -> vision-1   (no double diversion)
bare `custom_alpha/beta-1`        -> beta-1     (raw refs unchanged)
```

The real OpenCode CLI, through the real launcher:

```
$ mcc-opencode models
…
mcc/mcc/best
mcc/mcc/cheap
mcc/mcc/good
mcc/mcc/medium
mcc/mcc/vision

$ mcc-opencode run -m mcc/mcc/best "say ok"
> build · mcc/best
ok from beta-1
```

Request-log rows from that server (`requested_model` · `harness` · resolved · `params`):

```
mcc/best     harness=opencode  resolved=custom_beta/beta-1     {'tier':'best','tier_source':'override','tier_harness':'opencode'}
mcc/best     harness=crush     resolved=custom_alpha/alpha-1   {'tier':'best','tier_source':'global','tier_harness':'crush'}
mcc/best     harness=script    resolved=custom_alpha/alpha-1   {'tier':'best','tier_source':'global','tier_harness':'script'}
anthropic/mcc/best  harness=opencode  chain=custom_alpha/alpha-1,custom_alpha/alpha-cheap  {'tier':'best','tier_source':'global',…}
mcc/vision   harness=opencode  resolved=custom_alpha/vision-1  {'tier':'vision','tier_source':'global','tier_harness':'opencode'}
mcc/best     harness=opencode  resolved=custom_beta/beta-cheap {'tier':'best','tier_source':'override','tier_harness':'opencode'}
claude-fable-5  harness=claude  chain=custom_alpha/alpha-1,…   {}   ← no tier keys, shape unchanged
custom_alpha/beta-1  harness=opencode  chain=custom_alpha/beta-1  {}
```

## Browser drive of the Tiers section

Chrome, `screenshots-tiers/01`–`05`. Override → the shared rail appears; a pointer drag promoted the
fallback and Save wrote it (`{"model":"custom_beta/beta-cheap","fallbacks":["custom_beta/beta-1"]}`)
and the very next request resolved to `beta-cheap`; Pause struck the row through and posted the
per-agent list, not `MODEL_PAUSED`; Revert to global deleted the entry. **Zero console errors** (the
one 404 in the log is my own diagnostic fetch of a wrong asset path, not the page). Footer stayed
"No changes" throughout — a tier rail never joins the settings diff.

**The browser check earned its keep.** jsdom passed and the grid did not wrap, but the rail's text
input kept its intrinsic ~223px width inside a `minmax(0, 1fr)` column that had shrunk to 62px in a
340px card, and drew straight over the Pause chip beside it — invisible to every test. Two scoped
CSS rules fix it: `width: 100%` on the input, and `grid-column: span 2` for a card whose Tiers block
is open (combobox 63px → 437px). Measured after: every `.route-node` and `.model-chain-row` is 40px
tall with five children on one line, identical to the Model Config rail, `scrollWidth ==
clientWidth`.

## Tests

New: `tests/application/test_routing_tiers.py` (21) · `tests/application/test_catalogue_tier_aliases.py`
(44, parametrised over all 12 serialisers) · `tests/config/test_harness_tiers.py` (9) ·
`tests/api/test_admin_harness_tier_routes.py` (7) · `tests/core/test_request_log_tier_rows.py` (4) ·
`tests/contracts/test_claude_aliases_unchanged_by_tiers.py` (3). Extended:
`tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py` +7 jsdom cases (**219 passing alone with `-n 0`**, was 212),
driven through `tests/api/admin_jsdom_harness.mjs`; `test_import_boundaries.py` gains
`test_config_mirrors_the_tier_vocabulary_it_cannot_import`; `test_settings_to_consumer_contract.py`
gains the `HARNESS_TIER_ALIASES` hop.

`test_serialiser_contract.py::test_no_serialiser_hard_codes_a_limit` passes **unchanged** — an alias
adds no key its source entry lacks, which is the mechanical consequence of copying the record rather
than building one.

Full suite with a redirected HOME: **8,923 passed**, 17 failed. Baseline on this machine is 14–15
(8 websearch env leaks + 6 PowerShell installer), plus
`test_provider_manager.py::test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`, which was
**verified failing on a clean `fork/main` checkout** before any of this landed. The 219 jsdom
"errors" in that run are the documented node-harness timeout under full parallel load; the file
passes 219/219 alone. All four static gates clean: `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `ty check`
(1,144 files, no diagnostics — verified against a pristine `fork/main` worktree, which is also
clean), suppression grep.

## Deviations from the spec

- **The alias carries its own ref**, not the primary's. The spec had `gateway_id = "mcc/best"` with
  `provider_model_ref` left as the primary's; that collides in the six serialisers that key their
  document on the bare ref and skip a duplicate, so the alias would have silently vanished from
  Codex, Command Code, OpenCode, Kilo, Pi and Kimi. It is now `provider_model_ref = "mcc/best"` and
  `gateway_id = "anthropic/mcc/best"`, which also gives both spellings from one record with no
  per-CLI code. `parse_model_name` still sees two segments and Pi's extension still accepts it.
- **`config` may not import `core`.** `test_import_boundaries.py` declares `config` a leaf, so
  `TIER_NAMESPACE` and the tier names are mirrored in `config/constants.py` and pinned equal to
  `core.tier_refs` in both directions — the pattern `FAILURE_KIND_NAMES` already uses.
- **Model Config is untouched**, per the decision taken up front; no `ROUTE_TIERS` change, so
  `test_admin_routing_view.py` and `test_deadline_hint_labels.py` needed nothing.
- **Tier edits do not join Apply.** The spec had them posting on the page's Apply; they are not env
  keys, and collecting them in `changedValues()` would post unknown keys to `/admin/api/config/apply`
  on every Apply and make the page read dirty from a section the dirty count cannot explain. Each
  tier row has its own Save; Pause posts immediately, exactly as it does on Model Config.
- **Per-harness catalogue builds are conditional.** The spec's "13 builds instead of 1" is done only
  for an agent that actually has overrides — which is none of them until somebody opens the section.
- **`mcc-opencode run -m mcc/best` is spelled `-m mcc/mcc/best`.** OpenCode's `-m` is
  `<provider>/<model>` and its provider id is `mcc`, so the tier is addressed `mcc/mcc/best`; the
  wire `model` value is `mcc/best`, which is what the log shows.

## Residual risks

- **The `:has()` selector for the two-column card.** Supported in every browser this dashboard
  targets, but it is the first use in `admin.css`; a browser without it renders the previous, cramped
  layout rather than a broken one.
- **A tier resolving to a model the catalogue does not list gets no entry.** Correct (an alias the
  picker cannot select is worse than none), but an operator who hides `MODEL` behind
  `MODEL_VISIBILITY_DENY` loses `mcc/best` from the pickers while the router keeps answering it.
  Documented, not reconciled.
- **`MODEL` vs `MODEL_FABLE` divergence.** An operator who sets them to different refs gets `mcc/best`
  on `MODEL` and Claude Code's `claude-fable-*` on `MODEL_FABLE`. Surfaced in the docs; deliberately
  not reconciled.
- **Per-harness reasoning overrides are out of scope.** A tier inherits `REASONING_OPUS`/`_SONNET`/
  `_HAIKU` from the route it names; Best and Vision have no per-route setting and fall through to the
  global policy, because `settings.py` defines exactly four.
- **Crush and Cline now open on `mcc/best` rather than on `MODEL`'s raw ref.** Deliberate and the
  point of `is_primary_route` moving, but it is the one behavioural change to an existing generated
  document.
- **Kimi Code's key reads `mcc/mcc/best`.** Ugly in one CLI's `--model` help, correct everywhere; the
  alternative was a per-serialiser exception that breaks the "pure function of the records" property
  this layer is built on.

commit.message:
feat(models): one picker entry per tier, in every coding agent

Claude Code has never had to name a model. It asks for `claude-sonnet-5` and MCC
maps that onto whatever `MODEL_SONNET` points at, so moving a route moves every
session already running on it. Every other coding agent had to name a concrete
`provider/model` ref, because that was the only thing that existed for it — and
the request log is blunt about the consequence. Across the whole 272,132-row
history the number of non-Claude-Code requests that ever named a tier-style
alias is **zero**: every coding-agent request named a concrete provider/model
ref, while 99.98% of Claude Code traffic names an alias and almost never a ref.
A model id typed into OpenCode's config a month ago is still that id today,
however many times the route it should have been following was moved.

Five names close that gap. `mcc/best`, `mcc/good`, `mcc/medium`, `mcc/cheap` and
`mcc/vision` are emitted at the head of the picker MCC generates for each of the
thirteen agents that carry a catalogue, and each one names a route rather than a
model: `MODEL`, `MODEL_OPUS`, `MODEL_SONNET`, `MODEL_HAIKU` and `MODEL_VISION`,
together with each route's own `_FALLBACKS` and `_PAUSED` list. Pointer
semantics all the way down — including the collapse. On a default install the
four optional routes are unset, so all five tiers resolve to `MODEL`, exactly as
`claude-opus-5` already does; MCC does not invent a distinct model for an unset
tier, because choosing one would be MCC choosing a model for the operator. The
card says "Same as global Opus — currently <ref>. MODEL_OPUS is unset, so it
follows MODEL." instead of hiding it.

Both wire spellings parse, because the fleet is genuinely split: Codex, Command
Code, OpenCode, Kilo, Pi and Kimi Code put the bare ref on the wire, and Cline,
Crush, Droid, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code and Aider put `anthropic/<ref>`. The tier
segment is matched exactly, never as a substring — the older `_matched_route` is
a substring match, and repeating that hazard with five more names would be a
routing bug nobody could see. The interception sits *before*
`_direct_provider_model`: `mcc/best` already "worked" by accident, resolving to
`MODEL` with no fallbacks, no pause and no trace in the log, so this replaces
that silent behaviour rather than layering a rule on top of it.

Any one agent can be given its own chain for one tier, and only that agent
moves. The store is `~/.fcc/harness_tiers.json`, written atomically and modelled
on `model_overrides.json` — three states per (agent, tier), and the middle one
is the point of the file: key absent means inherit the global chain, an entry
with no `model` keeps the global primary and uses that agent's own fallbacks,
and a `model` set means that agent's chain leads. 195 `Settings` fields would
have been the alternative, which is not a manifest but a second product. The
per-agent half needs the request's harness identity (6.37.0); when the harness
is unknown — a raw curl, an old launcher — the tier still resolves, it simply
resolves globally.

The Coding agents card gains a Tiers section that renders the *same* rail
component Model Config uses, so the grip, the pointer drag, the move buttons,
the Pause button and the chain editor cannot drift apart from the ones beside
them. Its inputs never join `changedValues()` — they are one entry in a JSON
document, not env keys — so the page's dirty state is untouched and the section
writes through two new loopback-only routes on `api/admin_harness_routes.py`,
which was GET-only until now.

The alias record is the primary's `CatalogueModel` copied verbatim, with only
its identity replaced. Every capability field, every `field_provenance` entry
and every `None` travels with it, so no serialiser has to know a tier exists and
no number is invented — a MIN across the chain was rejected explicitly as a
number no source ever stated. It carries its own ref rather than the primary's
because the six agents that key their document on the bare ref would otherwise
dedupe the alias away against the model it points at.

Three consequences worth naming. `BEST` carries `is_primary_route`, so
`select_starting_index` seeds Cline's session model and Crush's `models.large`
on `mcc/best` with no change to that function — a session now opens on the route
rather than freezing today's answer into the agent's own config file. Crush's
`models.small` finally has an honest answer in `mcc/cheap`; it used to repeat
`large`, because inventing a cheap model by matching on a name would have been a
guess, and `mcc/cheap` is not a guess. And Gemini CLI's seeded model was a live
instance of the enumeration-artefact bug `core/catalogue_refs` was written to
kill — it never called `starting_model` and never read `MODEL`, pinning whichever
entry enumerated first — which is fixed here rather than left as an accident the
aliases happened to cover.

`MODEL_VISIBILITY_ALLOW/DENY` never filter a tier: filtering one would not hide
a model, it would remove the id an agent's generated config already names and
break its next session — the same exemption the eight `claude-*` names carry.
`HARNESS_TIER_ALIASES=false` is the supported way to shorten a picker, and the
router still answers an alias a client sends anyway. Claude Code is untouched:
it has no generated catalogue and keeps speaking its own alias names. The
provider id `mcc` is now reserved so a custom provider cannot shadow the
namespace. The request log records `tier`, `tier_source` and `tier_harness` in
`params` for a tier request only — no schema change, no export change — because
`requested_model` and `resolved_model` cannot answer "did my override fire?"
between them.
